subject.title: fix(cron): allow timeoutSeconds: 0 for no-timeout mode

question: Should the Control UI expose the existing `timeoutSeconds: 0` no-timeout cron sentinel despite the availability risk of user-configured runs without a watchdog?
rationale: The gateway/runtime contract already supports zero, but merging this PR makes the no-timeout mode reachable from the UI and can let scheduled work run indefinitely if misused.

options.title: Expose zero with proof
options.body: Refresh the PR onto the current cron module, add regression coverage, and require real UI proof before accepting the availability tradeoff.

options.title: Keep UI positive-only
options.body: Close or redirect the PR if maintainers want the no-timeout sentinel to remain API/CLI-only rather than visible in Control UI.

options.title: Expose with an explicit guard
options.body: Accept zero only with additional UI copy or confirmation so users understand they are disabling watchdog protection.

recommendation.title: Expose zero with proof
recommendation.body: Refresh the PR onto the current cron module, add regression coverage, and require real UI proof before accepting the availability tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: The cron edit parity work introduced the affected Control UI validation and payload behavior, making this the strongest feature-history routing signal.
